bihar_raw_news.content: Govt names 1993-batch IAS officer Poundrik as heavy industries secretary Poundrik's appointment comes at a time when crucial tasks for the heavy industries ministry would be to ensure smooth continuation of key electric mobility schemes such as the ₹ 25,938-crore production-linked incentive scheme for automobiles and auto parts and the ₹ 11,900-crore PM E-Drive scheme. Manas Pimpalkhare Published 30 Oct 2026, 09:23 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Poundrik, an IAS officer of the Bihar cadre, has been given additional charge of the heavy industries ministry while continuing as secretary of the steel ministry. AI Quick Read NEW DELHI: The appointments committee of the cabinet on Friday named 1993-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Sandeep Poundrik as secretary of the ministry of heavy industries, according to an official order. Poundrik, an IAS officer of the Bihar cadre, has been given additional charge of the heavy industries ministry while continuing as secretary of the steel ministry. Union minister HD Kumaraswamy holds both the steel and heavy industries portfolios, and Poundrik's new responsibility means he will now head both ministries at the secretary level. Also Read | Who is IAS Shalini Pandit, empanelled for Additional Secretary-level posts Poundrik's appointment comes at a time when crucial tasks for the heavy industries ministry would be to ensure smooth continuation of key electric mobility schemes such as the ₹ 25,938-crore production-linked incentive scheme for automobiles and auto parts (PLI Auto) and the ₹ 11,900-crore PM E-Drive scheme, while also ensuring that crucial advanced chemistry cell projects under the ₹ 18,100-crore PLI scheme for advanced chemistry cells (PLI ACC) scheme takes off successfully. The ministry also oversees operations at state-run Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (Bhel), an integral engineering and infrastructure sector public enterprise, which makes power generation equipment, transportation and railway equipment, defence and aerospace sector manufacturing, and clean energy products. The ministry is also responsible for running the ₹ 1,207 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector - Phase II, under which the government runs industry accelerators and skilling programmes to reduce gaps in research and development in the capital goods sector. Also Read | Meet Suhas Yathiraj: The IAS carrying India's hopes at Para Asian Games 2026 In November 2025, the heavy industries ministry also launched a ₹ 7,280-crore incentive package to set up five rare earth magnet making plants in the country, in the wake of a global rare earth magnet shortage caused by Chinese export controls in retaliation to steep US tariffs. Rare earth magnets are made from monazite deposits, of which India is the world's third largest source. These magnets are made after processing monazite --- China controls around 60% of the world's rare earth mining and 90% of the world's rare earth processing capacity --- and these magnets are used in crucial manufacturing sectors such as defence, electronics, renewable energy, and automobiles including cleaner electric vehicles. bihar_raw_news.title: 'Mothers of Courage,' documentary on girls' education in Bihar , wins UN SDG Action Award
bihar_raw_news.content: Shikshagraha, supported by Bengaluru-based non-profits ShikshaLokam and Mantra4Change, brings together more than 40 partner organisations across 16 states and Union Territories to strengthen public education and improve learning outcomes in government schools. Bengaluru: Mothers of Courage , a documentary on a grassroots movement led by women to promote girls’ education in Bihar, has won the 2026 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Action Award in the Creativity category. The documentary, part of Shikshagraha, a public education movement championed by Infosys cofounder SD Shibulal, was selected from more than 7,000 applications received from 190 countries and territories. The award was presented at a ceremony in Rome on Thursday. The initiative has mobilised over 1.19 million citizens across 14 districts in Bihar, where mothers and other women are challenging social norms that often prevent girls from completing their education. The film documents how some women are working to keep their daughters in school, while others are supporting their daughters-in-law in resuming their studies. Shikshagraha, supported by Bengaluru-based non-profits ShikshaLokam and Mantra4Change , brings together more than 40 partner organisations across 16 states and Union Territories to strengthen public education and improve learning outcomes in government schools. “This recognition goes beyond an award for a film or a campaign. It is a celebration of community-led transformation in education,” Shibulal, who is also the founder of ShikshaLokam, said. Live Events He added that lasting change in public education required coordinated efforts by governments, civil society, communities and philanthropy, with greater agency for those closest to children. At the centre of the Bihar initiative are Shiksha Chaupals, village-level community gatherings where women, parents and other residents discuss barriers to girls’ education, including child marriage, and collectively identify solutions. Since October 2024, more than 50,000 such gatherings have been held across rural India, encouraging communities to make commitments towards keeping girls in school and preventing early marriage. Similar gatherings have also begun in Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, and Odisha. Khushboo Awasthi , co-founder of Mantra4Change and chief curator of Shikshagraha, received the award in Rome. Recalling her own upbringing in a small Indian town, Awasthi said her mother had played a crucial role in helping her overcome social expectations surrounding education and career choices. “The women featured in Mothers of Courage are doing the same for their daughters and daughters-in-law. They are challenging deeply held beliefs, questioning established norms and changing what is possible for the next generation,” she said. Awasthi also acknowledged Urmila Kumari, a grassroots social reformer and Shikshagraha’s state head in Bihar, for her role in the movement. Kumari said the UN recognition belonged to the thousands of women and adolescent girls working to advance education and girls’ rights in rural communities. “This honour belongs not to any one organisation or team, but to the thousands of women and adolescent girls whose courage and determination have driven the fight for girls’ education and rights,” she said. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Transport Minister orders show-cause notices to DTOs over poor revenue collection
bihar_raw_news.content: National Bihar Transport Minister orders show-cause notices to DTOs over poor revenue collection On Oct 30, 2026 Share Patna, Oct 30 (IANS) Bihar Transport Minister Damodar Raut has directed the issuance of show-cause notices to more than 10 District Transport Officers (DTOs) for failing to achieve their assigned revenue collection targets. The directive was issued during a review meeting with DTOs held on Friday at the Bihar State Road Transport Corporation auditorium in Phulwari Sharif, Patna. The meeting reviewed revenue collection, road safety and the functioning of the transport system. During the review, the Minister was informed that revenue collection in several districts was below 40 per cent of the assigned targets. These included Munger, Kaimur, Saran, Jehanabad, Madhepura, Lakhisarai, Nawada, Buxar, Khagaria and Saharsa. Raut directed the concerned DTOs to explain their performance and instructed all officers to visit the field personally to accelerate revenue collection and achieve the targets. To improve transparency in enforcement activities, he also directed that body-worn cameras be provided to Enforcement Sub-Inspectors (ESIs) deployed at key checkposts, including those in Nawada, Kaimur, Gaya and Gopalganj. In view of the upcoming Diwali and Chhath festivals, the Minister instructed officials to keep a strict watch on buses to prevent overloading and ensure passenger safety. He also directed a complete crackdown on ‘jugaad’ vehicles and ordered a month-long special drive to seize vehicles operating without valid Registration Certificates (RCs). The Minister asked officials to expedite pending driving licence (DL) applications and directed the agency concerned to resolve complaints about the poor quality of driving licence cards within 15 days. He also called for speeding up ongoing projects, including the construction of driving training schools and bus stands, along with road safety initiatives. On hit-and-run cases, Raut instructed DTOs to deal with victims and their families sensitively and ensure that they receive benefits under government welfare schemes without delay or unnecessary difficulties. Emphasising the need to reduce road accident fatalities, the Minister directed officials to widely publicise the Pradhan Mantri Rahat Yojana, which provides cashless medical treatment to road accident victims. He stressed the need to inform people about hospitals registered under the Ayushman Bharat scheme. For effective implementation, DTOs were asked to coordinate with District Magistrates and the scheme’s nodal officers. The Minister also suggested creating awareness at police stations so that personnel could help accident victims gain admission to hospitals empanelled under the scheme. During the meeting, Raut also inaugurated a selfie point named ‘I Love Patna DTO’ outside the Patna DTO office. Senior officials present included Transport Department Secretary Raj Kumar, State Transport Commissioner Arif Ahsan and Additional Secretary Praveen Kumar. –IANS ajk/dan Share Facebook Twitter Google+ ReddIt WhatsApp Pinterest Email

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet Approves ₹37.10 Crore for Consultancy Services for Road Corridors
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Cabinet Approves ₹37.10 Crore for Consultancy Services for Road Corridors 30 Oct 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Bihar Cabinet approved ₹37.10 crore for transaction-adviser consultancy services for developing Vishwamitra Path, Ganga Ambika Path and Narayani Path under the PPP model. Key Points Road Infrastructure Projects: The three proposed road corridors—Vishwamitra Path, Ganga Ambika Path and Narayani Path—will have a combined length of approximately 220 km. These four-lane greenfield corridors are planned along the Ganga and Gandak river regions and will be implemented through the Bihar State Road Development Corporation Limited (BSRDCL) under the PPP model. Vishwamitra Path: A proposed 90-km road connecting Maner to Buxar via Ara. Ganga Ambika Path: A 56-km road connecting Bidupur and Dighwara. Narayani Path: A 73.51-km road project linked to Dubouli Ghat in Gopalganj district. Supaul–Araria Railway Line: The Cabinet approved the transfer of state government land to the Ministry of Railways to facilitate the construction of the new railway line. Approximately 3.13 acres in Pipra (Supaul district) and 21.48 acres in the Triveniganj–Pipra area have been approved for transfer. The proposed payments for the land are ₹66.97 lakh and ₹4.22 crore, respectively. Bihar State Road Development Corporation Limited (BSRDCL): It is a Government of Bihar undertaking responsible for the development, construction, improvement and maintenance of roads, highways, bridges and other related infrastructure. It implements road infrastructure projects through different modes, including PPP, Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) and externally assisted projects. Public-Private Partnership (PPP): PPP refers to a contractual arrangement between the government and private-sector entities for the development and delivery of public infrastructure and services. It facilitates private-sector participation in infrastructure development through investment, technical expertise and project management, while sharing project-related responsibilities and risks. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet Approves 43 Proposals, Including ₹11,096 Crore Power Distribution Plan
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Cabinet Approves 43 Proposals, Including ₹11,096 Crore Power Distribution Plan 30 Oct 2026 4 min read Why in News? The Bihar Cabinet , chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary , approved 43 proposals covering electricity distribution, urban infrastructure, flood management, industrial development, MSMEs, education, sports and regional air connectivity. Key Points Electricity Distribution: The Cabinet approved ₹11,096.55 crore to strengthen Bihar's low-tension electricity distribution network and upgrade cables, overloaded transformers and related infrastructure. The scheme will be implemented in phases over a maximum period of three years. Floodplain Mapping: A Flood Plain Zone Delineation Study will be conducted along the Kosi, Gandak and Son rivers to identify and map flood-prone areas. Study Cost: The floodplain mapping study will cost ₹1.99 crore and will be conducted under an MoU between Bihar's Water Resources Department and the National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee . Dam Safety Assessment: The Cabinet approved ₹8.39 crore for safety assessments of 24 dams in Bihar under the Dam Safety Act, 2021 . Patna Underground Road Corridor: An amount of ₹18.21 crore was approved for a feasibility study of an underground road corridor in Patna. Bihar State Games 2026: The Cabinet sanctioned ₹12 crore for organising the Bihar State Games 2026. Greenfield Satellite Townships: Restrictions on the purchase, sale and transfer of land in selected Greenfield Satellite Township areas were lifted with immediate effect. Bihar MSME Policy 2026: The Cabinet granted ex-post facto approval to the Bihar MSME Policy 2026 , which aims to transform one crore families into entrepreneurial households , generate one crore direct and indirect employment opportunities and raise the state's credit-deposit ratio to 75% . MSME Infrastructure: The policy envisages establishing an industrial cluster in every district and MSME centres in all 38 districts of Bihar. Motipur Sugar Mill Land: The Cabinet approved the transfer of 151.58 acres of land at the closed Motipur Sugar Mill in Muzaffarpur to the Industries Department for industrial development. Road Project Consultancy: An amount of ₹37.10 crore was approved for transaction adviser consultancy services for three proposed road projects: Vishwamitra Path: Buxar–Ara–Maner (90 km). Ganga Ambika Path: Bidupur–Dighwara (56 km). Narayani Path: Darihara (Konhua)–Dumariaghat in Gopalganj district (73.51 km). Regional Air Connectivity: An amount of ₹43.50 crore was approved as viability gap funding under the UDAN scheme . The funding will be provided to the Airports Authority of India for 29 months, from May 2026 to September 2028. Police Administration: Three City Superintendent of Police posts were approved for Motihari, Purnia and Saran districts. Economic Offences Unit: The Cabinet sanctioned 143 posts for expanding and strengthening regional Economic Offences Unit offices in Bihar. Bihar Information Commission: One post of State Information Commissioner was approved. Commercial Courts: Two District Judge-level posts were approved for additional commercial courts under the Patna judgeship. These courts will hear commercial disputes involving amounts exceeding ₹1 crore . bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet Approves Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026 - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Cabinet Approves Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026 30 Oct 2026 3 min read Why in News? The Bihar Cabinet approved the Bihar Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy 2026 to attract AI investment, promote startups and strengthen AI-based governance in the state. Key Points Objectives: Promote AI-driven governance, innovation, research, investment and skilled employment in Bihar. Attract AI companies, startups and Global Capability Centres (GCCs) . Financial Incentives: Capital investment and interest subsidies. Cloud infrastructure, lease rental and power tariff subsidies. Employment generation incentives, including ESI and EPF support. Certification reimbursement, AI model development and export incentives. Tailor-made incentive packages for eligible units. Startup and Research Support: Incubation, financial assistance, mentoring and market access for AI startups. Establish Centres of Excellence (CoEs) and promote industry-academia collaboration. Develop innovation hubs, data and computing facilities and IT parks. Priority Sectors for AI Adoption: Governance, agriculture, healthcare, education, manufacturing and urban services. Skill Development: Develop an AI-skilled workforce and promote digital entrepreneurship to generate high-value employment. India-AI Impact Summit 2026 About: Held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, India, in February 2026 , it brought the global AI summit series to the Global South . Its motto was "Sarvajana Hitaya, Sarvajana Sukhaya" (Welfare for all, happiness for all). Three Sutras, i.e., People, Planet and Progress, promoted inclusive, sustainable and development-oriented artificial intelligence. Seven Chakras: Priorities included Human Capital Inclusion for Social Empowerment Safe and Trusted AI Science Resilience, Innovation and Efficiency Democratizing AI Resources AI for Economic Growth and Social Good. Global Consensus: The New Delhi Declaration secured endorsement from 92 countries and international organisations , supporting equitable access and cooperation. Key Outcomes: Initiatives included the Global AI Impact Commons , Trusted AI Commons and Equitable AI Transition Playbook , promoting practical applications and workforce preparedness. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar MLC polls: RJD's Anil Jha declared elected, party's overall tally climbs to 17
bihar_raw_news.content: नवभारतटाइम्स.कॉम Anil Jha The Election Commission on Friday formally declared RJD candidate Anil Jha as elected from the Darbhanga Graduates constituency of the Bihar Legislative Council, where protracted counting of votes had raised the hackles of the opposition party. According to a statement issued by the EC, Jha secured 25,406 votes to wrest the seat from BJP MLC Sarvesh Kumar , who was the runner-up with a tally of 21,396 votes. In the biennial polls held on October 23 for eight constituencies, the RJD, which held none of these, has thus improved its overall tally in the Upper House by wresting two seats from the BJP, barely a year after suffering a humiliating defeat in assembly elections. Earlier, RJD candidate Sanjeev Kumar had been declared elected from Patna Teachers constituency, where he defeated five-term BJP MLC Nawal Kishor Yadav. Counting of votes had begun on Tuesday morning for all the constituencies. Live Events In Darbhanga Graduates seat, BJP supporters claimed a day later that the sitting MLC, whose tenure ends in November, has retained the seat. However, as counting of votes continued on Thursday, RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav, who is also the leader of the opposition in the state assembly, raised an alarm. In a post on X, the former deputy chief minister had accused the Election Commission of "foul play" and "trying to forcibly engineer a BJP victory" where "10 per cent of votes were declared invalid" during the counting process that took more than "56 hours". By late Thursday evening, when the counting of votes was complete for the constituency, though results were not formally declared, celebrations erupted in the RJD camp and Yadav, too, extended greetings to Jha. In the 75-strong legislative council, the BJP's tally has now fallen to 24, though it remains the single largest party in the Upper House. The party had contested four of the eight poll-bound seats, of which it held three. Though it lost Darbhanga Graduates and Patna Teachers, it wrested the Tirhut Teachers constituency, where BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh defeated CPI MLC Sanjay Kumar Singh. BJP's ally JD(U) retains the second spot in the Upper House, where it had 20 members. JD(U) MLC retained Patna Graduates for the fourth consecutive term. The party failed to win any of the remaining three seats that it had contested. The RJD remains the third largest party in the Vidhan Parishad, but with a slightly improved tally of 17, and Yadav has claimed that the results of the four Teachers and as many Graduates constituencies were "a mandate of the educated society against the NDA". bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Museum ranks 9th globally, beats Louvre and Met Museum - The Siasat Daily
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Lifestyle Lifestyle Bihar Museum ranks 9th globally, beats Louvre and Met Museum Bihar Museum's world-class recognition stems from its vast collection of artefacts Image Source: X In a historic global debut, the Bihar Museum in Patna has entered the top ten of the World’s 100 Best Museums 2026 ranking released by Munich-based travel publication Worth a Journey. Ranking first in Asia and ninth globally, it stands as the sole Indian cultural institution featured on the prestigious international list. The 2026 assessment, which combines worldwide data analysis with on-site evaluations, placed the Patna landmark ahead of world-renowned institutions. Notably, it outranked New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art, which placed tenth, as well as Paris’s iconic Louvre Museum , which was ranked 31st. Mexico City’s Museo Nacional de Antropología claimed the overall top spot. Spanning over 13 acres on Bailey Road, the state-of-the-art facility was designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki in collaboration with Mumbai’s Opolis Architects. The museum’s world-class recognition stems from its vast collection of artefacts spanning early human civilisations up to 1764, alongside its immersive spatial layout. Among its premier highlights is the Didarganj Yakshi , a life-sized Mauryan sculpture carved from polished Chunar sandstone, widely regarded as the crown jewel of the collection. Three expansive Historical Art Galleries trace regional history through the Indus Valley Civilisation, the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka, the Gupta Golden Age, and the reign of Sher Shah Suri. Visitors can also view the famous Kurkihar bronzes from the Pala dynasty, Kushan stone carvings, and punch-marked silver coins displayed in visible storage sections. In addition to ancient antiquities, Bihar Museum features an interactive Children’s Gallery complete with hands-on discovery zones, alongside specialised spaces celebrating Madhubani folk art and the global journey of the Bihari diaspora. Cultural historians and tourism officials have welcomed the global recognition, citing it as a major boost for heritage preservation and regional tourism infrastructure. The achievement highlights the institution’s role in showcasing India ‘s artistic legacy on an international stage. bihar_raw_news.content: Updated 30 October 2026 at 18:26 IST The ranking positions Bihar Museum ahead of New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art (10th) and well ahead of Paris’s Louvre (31st). Mexico City’s Museo Nacional de Antropología leads the global list, followed by Madrid’s Museo del Prado (2nd) and Denmark’s Louisiana Museum of Modern Art (3rd). Ankita Paul Global News 2 min read Follow : Global Spotlight on India as Bihar Museum Ranks 9th in the World, Tops Asia, Ahead of New York’s Met and Paris’s Louvre | Image: Social Media New Delhi: Patna’s Bihar Museum has secured the ninth position in the “World’s 100 Best Museums 2026” ranking published by the Munich-based independent travel guide Worth a Journey. The placement makes it the highest-ranked museum in Asia and the only Indian institution to appear in the top 100. The ranking positions Bihar Museum ahead of New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art (10th) and well ahead of Paris’s Louvre (31st). Mexico City’s Museo Nacional de Antropología leads the global list, followed by Madrid’s Museo del Prado (2nd) and Denmark’s Louisiana Museum of Modern Art (3rd). The State Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg and Vienna’s Kunsthistorisches Museum complete the top five. Worth a Journey compiles its lists using a proprietary algorithm that analyses large volumes of visitor data and reviews, combined with on-site expert evaluations. The guide covers museums of art, history, science, technology and open-air heritage. Opened in 2015 (with full operations by 2017) on a more than 13-acre campus on Bailey Road in Patna, the museum was designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki in collaboration with Mumbai-based Opolis Architects. It presents Bihar’s history from the Stone Age to more recent periods through chronological galleries featuring sculptures, coins, manuscripts, prehistoric tools and regional folk art, along with open courtyards, lawns and a dedicated Children’s Gallery. Advertisement Among its most celebrated holdings is the Didarganj Yakshi, a highly polished Mauryan-era sandstone sculpture discovered near Patna in 1917. The collection also includes Kurkihar bronzes and other significant artefacts. Celebrating the success, the Ministry of Culture, in a post on X, wrote, "A treasure trove of Bihar’s history and heritage, the museum houses ancient artefacts, sculptures, manuscripts and Mauryan-era relics, including a life-size Ashokan pillar. With interactive exhibits and well-curated galleries, it offers visitors an engaging journey through the rich history and cultural legacy of Bihar." Advertisement The achievement has drawn international attention to Bihar’s archaeological and artistic legacy, positioning the relatively young museum among the world’s elite cultural destinations.

Bihar Sponge Iron Limited has received a notice from the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi regarding an arbitration matter involving Vanraj Steels Private Limited. The hearing for the petition is scheduled for November 19, 2026. The company disclosed the development to BSE Limited pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The notice was received on October 29, 2026, and relates to Arbitration Petition No. 1671/2026. Nature of the legal proceeding Vanraj Steels Private Limited filed a petition under Section 11(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. This section pertains to the appointment of arbitrators by the court when parties fail to agree on the procedure. The petition arises from an existing arbitration agreement between the two entities. The High Court's notice requires Bihar Sponge Iron to show cause as to why the arbitration agreement should not be filed before the Court. This procedural step is standard in disputes where one party seeks judicial intervention to initiate or enforce arbitration proceedings. Key details of the disclosure Detail Information Petitioner Vanraj Steels Private Limited Respondent Bihar Sponge Iron Limited Case Number ARB. P. No. 1671/2026 Court Hon'ble High Court of Delhi Date of Notice Receipt October 29, 2026 Next Hearing Date November 19, 2026 The company stated that this disclosure is for information and records purposes. No financial impact or specific monetary claim amount was disclosed in the filing. bihar_raw_news.title: Cyclone Arnab puts two Bihar districts on red alert; weather warnings issued for others
bihar_raw_news.content: (File Photo: IANS) India 30th October 2026 Patna, October 30 (IANS) The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued weather warnings for several districts of Bihar on Friday under the impact of Cyclone Arnab, forecasting heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. A red alert has been issued for Sitamarhi and Madhubani, where extremely heavy rainfall and lightning are likely. An orange alert has been issued for Darbhanga, Sheohar, East Champaran and West Champaran, with heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and strong winds of 40-50 kmph expected. Yellow alerts have been issued for several other districts, including Patna, warning of rain, thunderstorms and lightning. Residents have been advised to remain alert and follow district-specific weather advisories. According to the Meteorological Centre in Patna, the impact of the weather system is expected to continue until October 31. The IMD has also forecast a significant decline in maximum temperatures in several parts of Bihar, with cooler conditions likely after the rainfall. The changing weather has brought an early winter-like chill to parts of the state. Patna, in particular, has witnessed a notable fall in temperature amid cloudy skies and intermittent rain. The weather department has cautioned that heavy rainfall could lead to waterlogging and disrupt normal movement in affected areas. Strong winds and lightning also pose risks to people working outdoors. Residents have been advised to take shelter inside safe, enclosed buildings during thunderstorms. They should avoid open fields, refrain from standing under trees and stay away from exposed locations during lightning activity. The Meteorological Centre has also urged people not to pay attention to rumours and to rely on official weather bulletins and government advisories for accurate information. The IMD's latest district-wise warning indicates that adverse weather conditions are likely to persist in parts of Bihar through Saturday, October 31. Cyclone Arnab has heavily disrupted normal life in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. The coastal areas of Odhisa, Jharkhand and Bihar are also affected by it.

bihar_raw_news.title: Canada tightens immigration rules , imposes fines of up to CAD 1.5 million
bihar_raw_news.content: Synopsis Canada has established new penalties for unauthorized immigration and citizenship advice, which will come into effect in 2026. Individuals providing paid immigration services must have proper authorization to avoid financial penalties. The penalties will range from CAD 5,000 for unauthorized advice to CAD 1.5 million for serious violations. Employers and applicants are advised to verify representative credentials and accuracy of information submitted. Listen to this article in summarized format Listen iStock Canada has introduced monetary penalties of up to CAD 1.5 million for violations involving unauthorised immigration and citizenship advice. The penalties also involve misrepresentation and deliberate submission of false or misleading information. The new rules, which came into effect on October 28, 2026, apply to both authorised and unauthorised representatives providing paid immigration or citizenship services, according to a Fragomen report. The penalties also cover individuals operating outside Canada. Also Read: US visa, green card applicants: What changed under USCIS filing deadline rules from October 23 Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) will also publish the names of penalised representatives and details of their violations in a public registry expected to be launched in 2027, on its official website. What do the new rules say? Under the new framework, individuals providing paid immigration or citizenship advice or representation without proper authorisation can face a fine of CAD 5,000. Also, individuals who knowingly provide false or misleading information on behalf of an applicant, or help an applicant submit such information, can face penalties of CAD 15,000. Also Read: Australia to tighten visa rules from October 31, with tougher character checks Additional penalties may apply if an immigration application is approved on the basis of false or misleading information. The amount of the penalty will depend on the seriousness and frequency of the violation, with the maximum amount reaching CAD 1.5 million for all violations combined. The rules cover paid representatives, including licensed immigration consultants, lawyers and other authorised representatives, as well as those offering such services without the required authorisation. What does this mean for employers and applicants? Employers managing immigration processes internally have been advised to review the activities of their teams and assess whether they require an authorised representative. Internal employees providing paid immigration advice or representation without the necessary authorisation could also face financial penalties and public disclosure of their violations. Employers and foreign nationals have also been advised to verify the credentials and authorisation of their immigration representatives and ensure that all information submitted as part of an application is accurate. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Museum in world's top 10, beats New York's Met and Louvre in Paris
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Museum in world’s top 10, beats New York’s Met and Louvre in Paris; Anand Mahindra calls it ‘game changer’ The list, published by Munich-based travel magazine Worth a Journey, also ranks the Patna museum first in Asia. Moneycontrol City Desk October 30, 2026 / 11:11 IST The Bihar Museum in Patna has been ranked ninth on the “World’s 100 Best Museums 2026” list, ahead of global giants such as the Louvre in Paris and New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art. The list, published by Munich-based travel magazine Worth a Journey, also ranks the Patna museum first in Asia. It is the only Indian museum in the top 100. The rankings are based on visitor reviews, data analytics and on-site evaluations by experts. This is a seminal moment of recognition. To have the Bihar Museum in Patna ranked 9th globally and the best in Asia is simply staggering. And it has the potential to be a game changer for the museum-going experience in India. Because it raises the bar for EVERY museum that exists in this country, and every museum yet to be built. A new gold standard. What makes this achievement even more remarkable is the story behind it. Conceived and championed by former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, & brought to life through the sustained efforts of the Bihar government and committed administrators. A great example of vision, administrative determination and world-class creative collaboration. The biggest beneficiaries will be the Indian public, who have long deserved museum experiences comparable to those they queue up for when travelling overseas. A standing ovation for EVERYONE who had a hand in making the Bihar Museum a reality. May this be the beginning of a museum renaissance in India… 👏🏽👏🏽👏🏽 — anand mahindra (@anandmahindra) October 29, 2026 Reacting on X, Mahindra Group chairman Anand Mahindra called it “a seminal moment of recognition,” and said it could be a game changer for the museum-going experience in India. Related Stories Bengaluru's Museum of Innovation, Startup & Technology to be designed by architects behind Grand Egy... Banana from multimillion-dollar artwork goes missing, French museum files complaint Karnataka approves AI Centre of Excellence in Electronics City; Transfer of 51% stake in Technology ... The ranking took many in the art world by surprise, given that the Bihar Museum is barely a decade old. The museum’s ‘Mona Lisa’ The Bihar Museum may not have the Mona Lisa, but it has its own showpiece: the Didarganj Yakshi, according to TOI. The life-sized, 2,000-year-old statue is carved from a single block of highly polished Chunar sandstone and stands in an air-conditioned room. Though her nose is chipped and her left arm broken, she holds a fly-whisk (chauri) in her hand. Spread over 13.9 acres, the museum also houses the famed Kurkihar bronzes, prehistoric stone tools, and a Kushan-period slab depicting the birth of the Buddha, the report said. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Drinking Water Project Gets Rs 1,774 Crore Backing - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Drinking Water Project Wins Rs 1,774 Crore NABARD Backing Breaking News Bihar Drinking Water Project Wins Rs 1,774 Crore NABARD Backing By Maria Dsouza October 30, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced a Rs 2,014 crore drinking water project for Aurangabad, Sasaram and Dehri, with Rs 1,774 crore approved by NABARD to upgrade water infrastructure under the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. The scheme will use surface water from the Sone river to strengthen existing supply systems in the three towns. The announcement was made by the chief minister on Thursday, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office. Choudhary said the project would expand drinking water facilities and improve water availability in the three areas. The state government said the scheme would initially serve a population of around 8 lakh. The project is expected to cover nearly 12 lakh people by 2051, indicating that the planned infrastructure is being designed around long-term population growth in the three towns. The announcement did not provide details of the proposed treatment capacity, distribution network, construction schedule, tendering process or commissioning date. The funding approved by NABARD is part of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund, which supports infrastructure projects through institutional financing. The statement did not specify how the remaining amount from the total project cost would be financed or provide a town-wise allocation for Aurangabad, Sasaram and Dehri. The proposed use of Sone river water will reinforce existing drinking water systems rather than replace them, according to the chief minister’s statement. The announcement therefore links the project to both source augmentation and the strengthening of civic supply infrastructure. Details on water treatment facilities, transmission lines, storage arrangements and household-level connections were not included in the information released. Choudhary also linked the initiative to Bihar’s Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali campaign, which promotes water conservation, environmental protection and the sustainable use of water resources. The project’s stated objective is to provide residents with clean and adequate drinking water while expanding the capacity of urban and surrounding supply systems. The announcement places the three towns within a wider state effort to improve basic infrastructure with support from the Union government and financial institutions. For residents, the eventual impact will depend on how quickly the approved funding is converted into construction, treatment and distribution capacity, as well as how the expanded network is operated and maintained. The Bihar government has not yet announced the project’s implementation timeline, construction milestones or completion date. Further details are expected as the scheme moves from funding approval to execution. national_raw_news.title: SEBI announces relaxation in KYC review rules for FPIs to boost ease of doing business 1 hour ago 154
national_raw_news.content: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has announced a significant relaxation in the Know Your Customer (KYC) review rules for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to boost the ease of doing business. Under the new guidelines issued today, the market regulator has increased the periodicity of KYC reviews for various categories of FPIs. As per the new guidelines, for Category-One FPIs from non-high-risk jurisdictions and certain high-risk entities registered under specific regulations, the KYC review will now be required only once every eight years instead of the earlier shorter timeline. For other FPI categories, including regulated entities and non-high-risk Category-Two investors, the review period has also been rationalised to every eight years, while remaining at every two years for certain remaining entities. In another major relief aimed at reducing the compliance burden, SEBI has completely dispensed with the requirement for FPIs to intimate changes in information or submit a no-change declaration at the time of continuing their registration. FPIs wishing to continue their registration for a subsequent block of three years will now only need to pay the required fees to their Designated Depository Participants (DDP) at least 15 days prior to the expiry of their validity. The regulator said that the KYC review timelines for FPIs investing exclusively in Government Securities and SWAGAT-FI FPIs will remain unchanged. These new provisions are set to come into force with effect from 1st December of this year.

national_raw_news.content: Home Minister Amit Shah today said the BJP would implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in Uttar Pradesh, expressing confidence that the party would return to power in the state after assembly elections next year. Addressing the BJP State Working Committee meeting in Lucknow today, he said the BJP government is as firm as Angad’s foot and could not be removed. He urged party workers to work with full commitment to secure another victory with a clear majority. He credited party workers for the BJP’s victories in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections. Mr. Shah said that the UCC has already been implemented in several states. Referring to 1990 firing on Ram devotees in Ayodhya during the Samajwadi party government, Mr. Shah alleged that indiscriminate firing had been ordered on devotees of Lord Ram and BJP workers. He claimed that the Samajwadi Party would remain out of power in the state for 30 years. The Home Minister lauded Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s contribution in the growth of the state saying that Uttar Pradesh has emerged as an investment hub, attracting investments worth over 50 lakh crore rupees. He added that improvements in law and order in UP had attracted investment, which in turn generated employment opportunities and eventually helped curb migration from the state. The meeting was chaired by BJP state president and Union Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, BJP state in-charge Vinod Tawde and national general secretary Smriti Irani and other members of the state executive committee attended the meeting.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two-day visit to Gujarat, beginning today. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 14 thousand crore rupees in Banaskantha today. The Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A (Airport Extension) and Phase-2B (GIFT City Extension). He will also release the 24th instalment under PM-KISAN, amounting to 19 thousand crore rupees. He will also visit the Embryo Transfer Technology-In Vitro Fertilisation Laboratory and the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre cattle farm in Banaskantha. The Centre will strengthen bovine breeding, genetic upgradation and advanced reproductive technologies, accelerating breed improvement by 10 to 20 times. Thereafter, the Prime Minister will travel to Ekta Nagar, Kevadia and inaugurate Bharat Parv 2026. Tomorrow, Prime Minister Modi will offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over four hundred crore rupees in Ekta Nagar. The projects include a sewage and water treatment plant, facade lighting, the upgradation of Narmada Ghat, and the Rainforest, among others. The Prime Minister will also participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

national_raw_news.title: 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang ANI | Updated: Oct 30, 2026 03:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 30 (ANI): The 14th edition of the International Tourism Mart (ITM), organised by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in association with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and other North Eastern States, commenced on Thursday at Tawang , Arunachal Pradesh . The three-day Mart, being held from October 29 to 31, aims to showcase the tourism potential of the eight North Eastern States and strengthen business engagement with domestic and international tourism markets. The inaugural session was held in the presence of Gajendra Singh Shekhawat , Union Minister for Tourism and Culture; Suresh Gopi, Union Minister of State for Tourism and Petroleum & Natural Gas; Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education and Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER); Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh ; and Prem Singh Tamang, Chief Minister of Sikkim. Tourism Ministers from the North Eastern States, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, international and domestic tourism stakeholders and representatives of the travel industry were also present. Addressing the inaugural session, Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat emphasised that the International Tourism Mart has evolved beyond a promotional platform into an important avenue for tourism partnerships and business opportunities. He stated, “ITM is not merely a tourism marketplace; it is a platform for building partnerships, generating business opportunities and creating a shared vision for the growth of tourism in the North East Region.” Highlighting the immense potential of the region, the Minister said that its rich biodiversity, cultural heritage, spiritual traditions and natural landscapes offer distinctive opportunities for adventure, nature-based and experiential tourism. He particularly emphasised the potential of adventure tourism, music festivals and concert tourism to attract new visitor segments, encourage longer stays and generate economic opportunities for local communities. He also called for developing tourism experiences with appropriate safety standards, community participation and environmental safeguards. The Minister highlighted the Government’s continued focus on improving connectivity, tourism infrastructure and destination experiences in the North Eastern Region. He also underlined the Ministry’s support for tourism promotion through domestic and international travel fairs, festivals, digital platforms and familiarisation visits, along with skill development initiatives to create employment opportunities for local youth. national_raw_news.content: India Post, UTI Mutual Fund extend partnership for doorstep KYC verification across India | Business About Career Advertisement Media Partnership Contact Us HOME NEWS RESEARCH LIVE DISCOURSE PERSPECTIVES AND INSIGHTS SUBMIT PRESS RELEASE NEWS DESK RESEARCH LIVE DISCOURSE PERSPECTIVES AND INSIGHTS INTERVIEW Home News Law & Governance Article India Post, UTI Mutual Fund extend partnership for doorstep KYC verification across India India Post and UTI Mutual Fund have extended their existing partnership to expand doorstep Know Your Customer (KYC) verification services for mutual fund investors across India, particularly in remote and underserved areas. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 21:10 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 21:10 IST Senior officials from the Department of Posts and UTI AMC during the meeting at UTI AMC’s Corporate Office (Photo/PIB). Image Credit: ANI SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... India Post and UTI Mutual Fund have extended their existing partnership to expand doorstep Know Your Customer (KYC) verification services for mutual fund investors across India, particularly in remote and underserved areas. According to a release issued by the Ministry of Communications on Thursday, the expanded collaboration aims to simplify investor verification, improve access to mutual fund services and strengthen financial inclusion. "Under the Pan-India KYC Verification Project, India Post will leverage its extensive postal network and last-mile connectivity to facilitate Know Your Customer (KYC) verification at investors' doorsteps, including in remote and underserved areas," the ministry said. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) extending the existing agreement was signed by Adnan Ahmed, Chief General Manager, Parcel & CCS Directorate, Department of Posts, and Vetri Subramaniam, Managing Director and CEO of UTI Asset Management Company Limited, in Mumbai on Thursday. The expanded partnership builds on an earlier KYC remediation initiative that helped investors complete pending verification requirements and address documentation gaps. "Building on the earlier KYC remediation initiative, which helped investors complete pending KYC requirements, improve compliance and address documentation gaps, the expanded collaboration is expected to strengthen investor servicing, encourage wider participation in mutual funds and support uninterrupted access to mutual fund investments," the release stated. India Post has already been providing doorstep KYC verification services for mutual fund investors. According to an earlier Ministry of Communications release issued in April 2025, India Post had completed over 5 lakh KYC verifications for UTI and the Specified Undertaking of the Unit Trust of India (SUUTI). The Department of Posts subsequently signed similar agreements with Nippon India Mutual Fund in April 2025 and SBI Mutual Fund later that month. In July 2025, India Post also entered into an agreement with the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) to facilitate KYC verification for mutual fund investors through its network of over 1.64 lakh post offices.
